title: Applied ML eval harness: prompt sets, model onboarding, quantization, and regression triage playbook
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Overview

This playbook defines Redwood Inference's cross-cutting applied-ML standards for: the eval harness onboarding flow, canonical prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and the regression triage process. The goal is predictable model quality and low operational overhead when introducing new model versions or quantized variants into serving.

Scope and audience
- Audience: ML Engineers, Applied ML, SREs supporting inference, and Platform Engineers who onboard models.
- Scope: Hosted, Dedicated, and Private serving paths; applies to curated open models and customer-requested custom variants.

Key definitions
- Eval harness: the automated pipeline that runs prompt sets, collects metrics, and generates pre-release quality reports.
- Prompt set: a curated collection of prompts grouped by capability, failure mode, and edge-case categories.
- Quantization profile: a configuration describing quantization approach (8-bit, 4-bit, per-channel/qkv-aware), and expected metric deltas.
- Regression: any measurable degradation in a tracked metric (accuracy, helpfulness, latency, safety) compared to the pinned baseline.

High-level SLOs and thresholds (applies to onboarding runs)
- Latency: p50 increase <= 10% and p99 increase <= 20% relative to baseline for single-request workloads.
- Throughput: sustained throughput drop <= 15% under identical batch configs.
- Quality (task-specific): absolute metric drop thresholds set per-prompt-set. Default thresholds: accuracy-style metrics <= 2% absolute drop; embedding cosine similarity decrease <= 0.02; helpfulness/regression alerts if human eval score drops >= 0.5 point on a 5-point scale.
- Safety: no increase in unsafe-response rate > 0.1% (measured on the safety prompt set).

Folder layout and required artifacts for onboarding
1) Model package (artifact registry): model-id, version tag, training provenance, tokenizer spec, and model config file (JSON).
2) Eval manifest (YAML): references to prompt sets, eval harness config, metrics to compute, baseline version id, and owners. Example snippet: 

---
model_id: "open-llama-70b"
version: "r1.quantint8"
prompt_sets:
  - "qa-core-general"
  - "safety-core"
  - "embedding-dataset-v1"
baseline_version: "open-llama-70b@r1"
metrics:
  - name: "qa_accuracy"
    threshold_abs_drop: 0.02
  - name: "embedding_cosine_mean"
    threshold_abs_drop: 0.02
owners: "team-applied-ml"
---

3) Quantization profile (if applicable): human-readable profile and machine-readable config. See section below.

Eval harness onboarding checklist (must be completed before canary rollout)
1. Create model package and upload to artifact registry. (Owner: model-onboarding engineer)
2. Add Eval manifest to eval-harness repo and create a PR referencing baseline. (Owner: applied-ml author)
3. Run full eval harness (100% prompt sets) in staging with identical serving config used in production. Attach run-id to PR.
4. Automated checks: compare metrics to baseline; enforce SLOs and per-prompt-set thresholds. Any hard-failure halts the pipeline.
5. Human review: for any metric within soft-failure window or for safety flag hits. Assign reviewers from the reviewers list.
6. Sign-off/approval PR merges and triggers canary deploy plan.

Prompt sets and benchmark guidance
- Naming: prompt sets use short, descriptive names (e.g., qa-core-general, summarization-news-2026, safety-core-1).
- Categorization: capability (QA, summarization), distribution (news, convo, code), difficulty buckets, and safety category.
- Minimum size: production prompt sets should contain >= 500 examples for statistical signal (smaller targeted sets are allowed for narrow capabilities).
- Benchmarks: include deterministic metrics (exact-match, F1), approximate metrics (BLEU/ROUGE), embedding metrics (cosine similarity), and human eval templates.
- Coverage matrix: each prompt set must document expected behavior and known acceptable variants (tie-breaker rules).

Quality guardrails (automated + human)
Automated guardrails:
- Pre-merge checks: metric diffs, resource usage (GPU memory/cold-start), safety classifier hits.
- Canary monitors: run online prompt-set probes (100 unique probes per hour) and measure response drift. Alert thresholds: >5% of probes with semantic drift OR >10% safety classifier increase -> automatic rollback.

Human guardrails:
- Ad-hoc human eval: run when any soft-failure occurs or for major model upgrades (>2x parameter increase or architecture changes).
- Explainability checks: sample KV-cache-related failures and hallucination cases.

Quantization profiles and recommended practices
- Profile fields required (machine-readable): profile_name, algorithm (PTQ, QAT), bitwidth, per_channel (true/false), calibrator_dataset, expected_metric_delta_map (metric->expected delta), fallback_strategy.
- Example profile (YAML):
---
profile_name: "int8-qkv-aware"
algorithm: "PTQ"
bitwidth: "8"
per_channel: true
calibrator_dataset: "calib-100k-rep"
expected_metric_delta_map:
  qa_accuracy: 0.01
  embedding_cosine_mean: 0.005
fallback_strategy: "use-original-weights-if-fallback"
---
- Guidance: start with per-channel 8-bit PTQ for transformer weights, evaluate attention qkv quantization separately (qkv-aware) and measure outputs on a focused prompt set. 4-bit quantization must include per-layer sensitivity analysis and is considered experimental unless signed off.
- Performance notes: include memory usage deltas, throughput change at batch sizes 1/4/16 and p50/p99 latency deltas. Document these as part of the quantization profile artifact.

Regression triage playbook (detailed flow)
1) Detection (automatic): regression alert fires from eval-harness nightly run or from canary monitors. Alert payload must include run_id, model_version, metric_name, current_value, baseline_value, delta, and top 5 failing prompt ids.
2) Triage owner assignment: alerts route to applied-ml on-call rotation. If severity=sev2 or higher, page SRE on-call.
3) Initial investigation (30 minutes):
   a) Reproduce: re-run the failing prompt-set locally against baseline and candidate with identical RNG seeds.
   b) Check infra signals: GPU memory errors, OOMs, non-deterministic CUDA kernel warnings, and library version mismatches.
   c) Check quantization profiles: if candidate is quantized, re-run unquantized variant to isolate quantization-induced regressions.
4) Root cause hypothesis (2 hours): produce a short hypothesis note and attach to the incident. Possible root causes: data-shift in prompts, tokenizer changes, model architecture changes, quantization rounding error, batching/ordering bug, or metric calculation change.
5) Mitigation options (ranked):
   - Rollback to baseline (fastest).
   - Serve fallback policy: route traffic to baseline for affected routes only.
   - Patch: fix metric calculation bug or tokenizer mismatch and trigger new eval run.
   - Re-quantize with adjusted profile.
6) Recovery and verification: after mitigation, run the full eval-harness and canary probes for 24 hours to validate stability.
7) Post-incident: write a short postmortem within 3 business days and update the model onboarding checklist if process gaps are found.

Severity definitions and response times
- Sev1: Safety-critical regression (unsafe outputs increased >0.5% absolute or PII leakage confirmed). Response: page on-call and execs; 0-30 minute ack.
- Sev2: Major quality regression (task metric drop >5% absolute or production user-visible error). Response: on-call ack within 60 minutes.
- Sev3: Minor regression or noise (failures not user-visible or within allowed thresholds). Response: track in ticket and prioritize.

Operational playbook snippets (commands & quick checks)
- Trigger a full eval run: python infra/eval_harness/run_eval.py --manifest path/to/manifest.yaml --output-dir /tmp/run-123
- Compare runs: python infra/eval_harness/compare_runs.py --baseline run-456 --candidate /tmp/run-123 --report /tmp/report.html
- Quick local quantization check: scripts/quant/check_quant_accuracy.sh open-llama-70b r1.quantint8 calib-100k-rep

Ownership and escalation
- Primary owners: team-applied-ml (model quality and eval harness), team-serving-runtime (latency and runtime regressions), team-eng-sre (on-call and capacity impacts).
- Escalation matrix: applied-ml -> serving-runtime -> eng-sre -> vp-eng (if unresolved after 8 business hours).

Governance and continuous improvement
- Quarterly audits: every quarter applied-ml will run an audit of top 25 prompt sets to identify drift and update calibration datasets.
- Playbook reviews: reviewers above should revalidate this playbook annually or after any Sev1/Sev2 regression.

Appendix: common failure modes and detection heuristics
- Tokenizer mismatch: symptoms = off-by-one tokenization; detection = tokenized length distribution shift > 5%.
- Non-deterministic kernels: symptoms = metric variance across repeated runs; detection = variance in metric > 2x expected CI.
- Quantization drift: symptoms = systematic embedding cosine decrease; detection = run embedding sanity set and compare distribution quantiles.
